patterns.note: Output hub uses sticky bounded scrolling in selected viewport/pointer modes, but current wide desktop and portrait-tablet guards intentionally fall back to static flow.

mechanism: Output hub remains a grid/flow participant rather than a fixed overlay.
A sticky variant constrains the pane with viewport-relative max-height and internal vertical scrolling.
Wide desktop fine-pointer mode intentionally switches .output-hub to position:static, max-height:none, overflow:visible to avoid nested scroll areas.
Portrait/narrow tablet guards also restore static flow instead of squeezing desktop columns.
implementation_effects: Supporting output/review content can remain nearby on layouts where sticky behavior is useful.
Wide desktop uses available page height naturally and avoids an unnecessary nested scrollbar.
Portrait tablet/desktop-site browser geometry collapses to a safe single-column layout.
Sticky behavior is independent from the preview dialog's actual backdrop-filter blur.
responsive_contract: Selected intermediate layouts may use sticky output-hub behavior with bounded overflow.
Desktop at min-width 1280px with hover/fine pointer uses static output flow.
Portrait tablet 601–1180px uses single-column static output flow.
limitations: This is a conditional/adaptive realization, not a claim that the output hub is sticky in every desktop state.
The earlier glass-like appearance must not be inferred as backdrop blur; actual backdrop-filter usage belongs to the preview dialog backdrop.
This record proves source behavior and tests, not a production screenshot.
